question_text: Quadrilateral PQRS has the measurements shown.

mark_breakdown.desc: Applying the cosine rule in triangle $PQR$

subparts.solution: By the cosine rule in $\Delta\text{PQR}$: $\text{PR}^2 = 3^2 + 12^2 - 2(3)(12)\cos 102^\circ \implies \text{PR} = \sqrt{3^2 + 12^2 - 2(3)(12)\cos 102^\circ} \implies \text{PR} \approx 12.96\text{ cm} \approx 13.0\text{ cm}$.

ai_explanation.concept_rule: The cosine rule finds an opposite side given two sides and an included angle: $c = \sqrt{a^2 + b^2 - 2ab\cos C}$.
step_by_step: Substitute side lengths $3$, $12$ and included angle $102^\circ$ into the cosine rule.
Compute the right-hand side carefully, noting $\cos 102^\circ < 0$.
Take the square root to get $\text{PR}$.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Mistakenly treating $\cos 102^\circ$ as positive or prematurely rounding intermediate values.

subparts.stem: Determine the measure of the angle marked $\theta$.

mark_breakdown.desc: Setting up the sine rule in triangle $PRS$

ai_explanation.concept_rule: Apply the sine rule $\frac{\sin\theta}{c} = \frac{\sin C}{s}$ using the calculated value from the previous subpart.
step_by_step: Set up the sine rule linking $\theta$ and $\text{PR}$, and $42^\circ$ with side $15$.
Substitute the unrounded or more accurate value of $\text{PR} \approx 12.96$.
Solve for $\theta$ by taking the inverse sine.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Using the rounded value $13.0$ instead of $12.96$, potentially causing rounding error in the final angle.
